steps.root: Every solution starts at the "solve" block. Whatever is plugged into "return" is the answer.

devolva-entrada.2: The "input" block (in Variables) holds the problem's value. Plugged into "return", it comes back unchanged — done.

e-par.2: In Logic, the "=" comparison answers true or false. Plugged straight into "return", it is already the answer.
e-par.3: On the left, "remainder of … ÷ …" (in Math): what is left over when dividing one number by the other.
e-par.4: The number to divide is the "input".
e-par.6: On the right, 0: if dividing by 2 leaves no remainder, the number is even.

soma-lista.2: In Variables, "Create variable..." creates "total", and "set total to" stores a value in it.
soma-lista.3: The total starts at 0: before adding any number, the sum is zero.
soma-lista.4: In Loops, "for each item numero in list" repeats what is inside once per item; on each pass, the variable "numero" holds the current item.
soma-lista.5: The list being walked through is the "input".
soma-lista.6: Inside the loop, another "set total to" replaces the total with a new value on every pass.
soma-lista.7: The new value is "total + numero": the sum so far plus the current number.
soma-lista.8: After the loop, "total" goes into "return": it is the sum of the whole list.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.intro: kumite is the block-programming platform for the competition between PUCRS and Universidad de Mérida.

what.title: What kumite is
what.body: A problem appears on screen and you solve it by dragging programming blocks. Your solution goes to the server, which runs it against test cases and scores it automatically.

teams.title: Teams
teams.body: You compete as a team, and the score belongs to the team. The organizers set the maximum team size and whether teams may mix students from both universities (by default, they may); the Teams screen shows the rules in force. Once your team has made its first submission, no one can leave it.

rounds.title: Rounds and scoring
rounds.body: The organizers open a round and a timer starts; when time runs out, the round closes. Each problem is worth a number of points, and a solution earns the share of them that matches the hidden test cases it passes: the visible examples are worth no points. Your team's best submission on each problem is the one that counts. On a tie, the team that reached its best scores sooner ranks higher (adding up, over each scored problem, the time since the round opened), then the one with fewer submissions.

editor.title: The block editor
editor.body: Every solution starts at the "solve" block: whatever you plug into "return" is the answer. Run tries your solution on the visible examples; during a round, Submit sends it to the judge.

practice.title: Where to practice
practice.body: The Practice tab has problems open at any time, with or without a round. There is no submission or scoring there: it is the place to get used to the blocks before the competition.
